cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Below is a summary of our cost of sales and gross margin, in thousands, for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025:

Cost of sales for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased 12.1% as compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in cost of sales is primarily due to higher automotive volumes, unfavorable foreign currency impacts primarily attributable to the Chinese Renminbi, Mexican Peso, Czech Koruna and the Euro, specific-cause warranty provisions related to products shipped in prior periods and higher labor costs, partially offset by material purchasing savings.

Below is a summary of our cost of sales and gross margin, in thousands, for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025:

Cost of sales for the six months ended June 30, 2026 increased 11.5% as compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in cost of sales is primarily due to higher automotive volumes, unfavorable foreign currency impacts primarily attributable to the Mexican Peso, Euro, Chinese Renminbi and the Czech Koruna, specific-cause warranty provisions related to products shipped in prior periods and higher labor costs, partially offset by material purchasing savings.

rd.heading: Net Research and Development Expenses
rd.text:
Below is a summary of our net research and development expenses, in thousands, for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025:

Net research and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased 6.7% as compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in net research and development expenses is primarily related to unfavorable foreign currency impacts primarily attributable to the Chinese Renminbi and the Euro and lower customer reimbursements.

Below is a summary of our net research and development expenses, in thousands, for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025:

Net research and development expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 increased 2.7% as compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in net research and development expenses is primarily related to unfavorable foreign currency impacts primarily attributable to the Euro and the Chinese Renminbi.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:

Merger and acquisition expenses, primarily related to the Modine Transaction, were $12.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The remaining increase in selling, general and administrative expenses is primarily related to higher expenses for information technology and unfavorable foreign currency impacts primarily attributable to the Mexican Peso, Euro and the Chinese Renminbi.

intro.text: Gentherm Incorporated, a Michigan corporation, and its consolidated subsidiaries (“Gentherm”, “we”, “us”, “our” or the “Company”) is a global market leader of innovative thermal management and pneumatic comfort technologies. Our automotive products include variable temperature Climate Control Seats (CCS®), Climate Control Interiors (CCI™), Lumbar and Massage Comfort Solutions, Valve Systems, and electronic solutions for climate and comfort technologies. Our automotive products can be found on light vehicles manufactured by nearly all the major original equipment manufacturers (“OEMs”) operating in North America and Europe, and several major OEMs in Asia. We operate in locations aligned with our major customers’ product strategies to provide locally enhanced design, integration and production capabilities.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
